chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu 'Ubaydah, who said:
One of our companions asked Aba 'Abdillah (عليه السلام) about al-Jafr, so he said: “It is an ox-hide filled with knowledge.”

He said to him, “Then al-Jami'ah?” He said: “That is a scroll whose length is seventy cubits, in the width of the tanned hide, like the thigh of the camel, containing everything the people need; and there is no legal case except that it is in it, even the compensation for a scratch.”
He said, “Then the Mushaf of Fatimah (عليها السلام)?” He said: So he remained silent for a long while, then said: “You indeed inquire into what you need and what you do not need.”

Fatimah (عليها السلام) remained after the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) for seventy-five days, and intense grief over her father entered upon her. Jibra'il (عليه السلام) used to come to her, console her excellently regarding her father, comfort her soul, inform her about her father and his place, and inform her of what would occur after her among her progeny; and 'Ali (عليه السلام) would write that down. So that is the Mushaf of Fatimah (عليها السلام).

key_terms.أَرْشُ الْخَدْشِ: The compensation due even for a minor bodily injury such as a scratch.
key_terms.الْجَامِعَةُ: A lengthy scroll containing all matters people need, including legal judgments.
key_terms.الْجَفْرِ: A skin container described here as being filled with knowledge.
key_terms.حُزْنٌ شَدِيدٌ: Intense grief felt by Fatimah (عليها السلام) after her father.
key_terms.قَضِيَّةٍ: A legal case or matter requiring judgment.
key_terms.مُصْحَفُ فَاطِمَةَ: The written record of what was conveyed to Fatimah (عليها السلام) after the passing of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله).

ai.seo_question: What is the Mushaf of Fatimah (عليها السلام) according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith describes three inherited repositories of knowledge associated with the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام): al-Jafr, al-Jami'ah, and the Mushaf of Fatimah (عليها السلام). It explains that the Mushaf of Fatimah (عليها السلام) consisted of what Jibra'il (عليه السلام) conveyed to console her after the passing of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), which Imam 'Ali (عليه السلام) wrote down. The report highlights the special knowledge entrusted to the Imams (عليهم السلام) and the unique rank of Sayyidah Fatimah (عليها السلام).

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked by one of our companions about the Jaf’r. So heasws said: ‘It is an ox hide filled with knowledge’.

He said to himasws, ‘So the Jami’e?’ Heasws said: ‘That is a lengthy Parchment of seventy cubits in width of the leather, like a thigh of the camel. Therein is everything what the people would be needy to, and there isn’t anything from a judgment except and it is therein, to the extent of the compensation for a scratch’.

He said, ‘So the Parchment of Syeda Fatima<sup>asws</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> was silent for a long while, then said: ‘You all are exploring about what you need and about that which you do not need!

Fatimaasws remained after Rasool-Allahsaww for seventy-five (75) days, and intense grief entered into herasws for herasws fathersaww, and it was so that Jibraeelas would come to herasws and would give condolences upon herasws fathersaww, and that would better herasws self, and heas informed herasws about herasws fathersaww, and hissaww place, and heas informed herasws with what would be happening after herasws in herasws children, and Aliasws would write that down. So this is the Parchment of Syeda Fatimaasws’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from abu ‘Ubaydah who has said that the people from our group asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about Jafr and the Imam (a.s.) said the following.
“It is the skin of a bull which is full of knowledge.” Then they asked the Imam (a.s.) about al-Jami‘a.

The Imam (a.s.) replied, “It is a parchment that is seventy yards long with a width of hide like that of the leg of a huge camel. It contains all that people may need. There is no case for there is a rule in it. In it there is the law to settle the compensation for a scratch caused to a person.”
The narrator has said that he asked the Imams (a.s.), “What is Mushaf of Fatima?” The Imam (a.s.) waited for quite a while.

Then he said, “You ask about what you really mean and what you do not mean. Fatima (a.s.) lived after the Messenger of Allah for seventy-five days. She was severely depressed because of the death of her father. Jibril (a.s.) would come to provide her solace because of the death of her father. Jibril would comfort her soul. Jibril would inform her about her father and his place and of the future events and about what will happen to her children. At the same time Ali (a.s.) would write all of them down and thus is Mushaf of Fatima (a.s.).”
